claims.text: Ask: what they're proud of; what's exciting about this stage; how the family is doing; what they enjoy and what seems most difficult about the child; major family changes or stressful events and their effect; questions or concerns.
claims.quote: What are you most proud of since our last visit? (If the parent responds, “Nothing,” the clinician should be prepared with a compliment, such as, “You made time for this visit despite your busy schedule.”) • What’s exciting about this stage of development? What do you like most about this age? • How are things going in your family? • Let’s talk about some of the things you most enjoy about your child. On the other hand, what seems most difficult? • What major changes have occurred in your family since your last visit? Tell me about any stressful events. What is the effect of these changes on your family? • What questions or concerns do you have about your child?
claims.locator: 2 year visit, Health Supervision: History / Review of Systems

claims.text: Past medical hx: any specialty or emergency care since the last visit.
claims.quote: received any specialty or emergency care since the last visit?
claims.locator: 2 year visit, Health Supervision: History / Review of Systems

claims.text: Family hx: any new health condition or death in the family; if yes, who has or had it, age at onset and diagnosis, or age at death.
claims.quote: developed a new health condition or died? If the answer is Yes: Ascertain who in the family has or had the condition, and ask about the age of onset and diagnosis. If the person is no longer living, ask about the age at the time of death.

claims.text: ROS — any problems with: head shape; vision or crossed eyes; ears, nose and throat; breathing or chest pain; nausea or vomiting, bowel movements; birthmarks or moles; muscle strength, movement or function; language.
